en: The Hymn to the Verses and Words of the Mantra of Medhādakṣiṇāmūrti.
"Om"—the three tufts [of hair] utter this single-syllabled Brahman.
Salutations to that Medhādakṣiṇāmūrti, whose nature is the Savior (Tārātman). 1
Having bowed to him, all these sages go to the supreme, unassailable state.
Salutations to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, whose form is the syllable *Na* and who bestows wisdom.
Released from the snare of delusion, the knower of Brahman attains that state.
Salutations to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the embodiment of wisdom, whose form is the syllable *mo*;
by taking refuge in whom, the wise man, having transcended worldly existence (*bhava*), became the supreme non-existence (*abhava*).
Salutations to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the embodiment of wisdom, whose form is the syllable *bha*.
The entire world shines as a delusion, like the form of the sky;
salutations to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, whose nature is the letter *ga* and who is the intellect.
Salutations to that imperishable Lord who dwells at the root of the banyan tree for the sake of the worlds.
To the one whose form is the syllable *va* ... 6.
He by whose splendors this sun becomes the ordainer of time—to the one whose form is the syllable *te* ... 7.
To Him who, in the destruction of Dakṣa and Tripura, and in the neutralizing of the poison of Kāla,
takes the form of the letter *Da*...
(8) By the mere remembrance of His name, men swiftly attain the perfection of speech (*vāk-siddhi*).
To the one whose form is the syllable *kṣi* ... 9.
He who is expressed by the syllable *ṇa* kindles my sleeping mind;
to the one whose form is the syllable *ṇa* ... 10.

To him whose eightfold forms are the cause of the birth and so forth of the universe, [salutations] to the one whose form is the syllable *mū*. 11. That you are the supreme reality, Brahman—this is what was taught to me by my guru.
Sarepha-tātmane me... 12.
Having known this, Brahmā and the other sages attain liberation; [salutation] to the one whose form is the syllable *ya*. 13.
The ignorant call the Great One "Deva" according to the *Nigamas* and *Āgamas*.
To Him who is in the form of the letter *Na*...
(14) He who stands pervading the entire universe, both within and without.
To the one whose form is the syllable *maka*...
15 You alone are the witness of the world, the cause of its creation, preservation, and end.
To the one whose form is the syllable *mekā*... 16

The syllable *dā* is said to be the cause and the effect of the creation of the Creator (*dhātṛ*). By meditating upon that which is beyond primordial nature (*prakṛti*) and which takes the form of the syllable *dhāṃ*, the sage indeed attains identity with it.
To Him whose form is the manifestation of all modes... 18 The wise worship Him who transcends the principles (tattvas) and whose nature is consciousness;
to Him whose form is the embodiment of knowledge... 19
For one who practices through various means such as meditation, worship, and so forth, wisdom is born;
by the mere remembrance of whom a person is liberated from all bonds.

The fire and the senses, having attained dullness toward their objects here in this world, [are offered] to the one whose form is the syllable *ya*... 21. The fire and the senses, having attained dullness toward their objects here in this world, [are offered] to the one whose form is the syllable *u*... 22.
To the one composed of consciousness who dwells afar from both the ignorant and the knowers within their own hearts;
to the one whose form is his own nature...
23 To the one for whom the lord of serpents serves as a necklace, and who bestows all branches of knowledge.
To the one whose form is the syllable *Hā* ... ॥ 24 ॥ Thus ends the "Hymn to the Verses and Words of the Mantra" of the venerable Medhādakṣiṇāmūrti.
